description: OpenHI (Open Hydrological Information, Greece) is a portal or repository of infrastructure or hazard data run by Hellenic Centre for Marine Research with 14 Greek universities and research institutions, coordinated from the National Technical University of Athens. OpenHI describes itself as open infrastructure for the surface waters of the country: telemetric measurements from monitoring stations in rivers, lakes and reservoirs, water quality parameters (pH, salinity, temperature, dissolved oxygen, conductivity), and derived discharge and statistics, shown in a web portal (system.openhi.net) with geographic datasets offered separately. Coverage: Greece, stations of the national hydrometric network. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is: free access according to the page; licence terms sit on a separate page that was not read. Caveats: the station network is still expanding and the page names one example station; download formats and the interface were not read. It can support river and reservoir monitoring for flood, drought and water-supply studies. Related records: no directly related record is catalogued yet; the data are reached through the portal page linked here.
